doc.title: Chuck Mancuso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 10, 2013

title: King Records chart and the hillbilly, pops and sepia categories
summary: Rowe asks about a King Records chart; Mancuso explains Cincinnati as a border town mixing country and rhythm and blues acts.

bands.name: Hank Penny and his Radio Cowboys

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: And I’m fascinated by the — you had one chart, it was almost like a poster, and it said King Records. It was a thing for King Records.
And it said “We sell in all three fields: Hillbilly, Pops and Sepia.” And it’s so informative to see that language.

Yeah. Because Cincinnati was, like a border town. They had the black part of town on one side, and they had the white part, so you had Moon Mulligan and Hank Penny and his Radio Cowboys, and then they had Wynonie Harris Going Wild. And oh my God.
